The curriculum approval process generally follows the sequence shown in the URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart. Specific steps may vary by college, department, proposal type, and whether the proposal requires additional levels of review.
URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart

Proposal Development Faculty use the forms in Kuali Curriculum Management to develop the proposal and work with other stakeholders as appropriate.
Department Review The proposal is reviewed through the appropriate departmental process.
College Curriculum Committee Review The College Curriculum Committee reviews the proposal.
College Dean Approval The College Dean approves the proposal for Faculty Senate review.
Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee Review The Curriculum & Standards Committee, the General Education Committee, or the Graduate Council reviews the proposal.
Faculty Senate Approval The Faculty Senate considers the curriculum committee's recommendation and votes.
University President Approval Any curricular item that is not a course must be reviewed and approved by the University President.
URI Board of Trustees Approval In addition to the University President’s approval, new Majors and Degrees are also reviewed by the Board of Trustees.

While all Colleges follow the curriculum approval process established in the University Manual, each College may have its own internal approval process based on its departmental and governance structures. To download a flowchart of a specific College’s approval process, select the College below.

Repeat Criteria
Tags: courses
Short Description: The criteria specifying how many times a course may be taken, the maximum credits that may be earned through repeated enrollment, and any restrictions on repeating the course within the same term.
Repeat Criteria
The criteria specifying the limits and conditions for repeating a course, including:
Maximum Enrollments: The maximum number of times a course may be taken.
Maximum Credits Allowed: The maximum number of credits that may be earned through repeated enrollment during a student’s academic career.
Same-Term Repeats: Whether the course may be repeated within the same term.
Maximum Credits Allowed Per Term: The maximum number of credits that may be taken through repeat enrollment in a single term.

Grand Challenge
Tags: courses
Short Description: A General Education overlay centered on a complex contemporary issue and designed to engage students through interdisciplinary perspectives and ethical inquiry.
Grand Challenge
A Grand Challenge course centers on a complex issue of contemporary significance and provides students with opportunities to explore, question, and critically engage with the issue. The course incorporates at least two disciplinary perspectives and helps students make interdisciplinary connections through assignments, activities, and/or experiences. It also addresses the ethical challenges associated with the issue, providing students with opportunities to apply ethical concepts or frameworks in evaluating potential actions and their ramifications.
Proposers will complete the Grand Challenge section in their Kuali Course Proposal. This Grand Challenge Template is available as a resource to help prepare responses for submission.
